title: Affinity bleed from delayed decommission caused tier overload and fallback cascade - postmortem
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-01 at ~07:42 UTC a subset of traffic converged on a single tier in us-west-2 which caused that tier to exceed healthy load and trigger aggressive fallbacks to lower-cost model variants across other regions. The cascade generated elevated tail latency, token errors, and a temporary 18-minute spike in 5xxs for affected customers.

Impact:
- Duration: ~18 minutes (07:42–08:00 UTC) with degraded slow requests lingering in traces until 08:15 UTC.
- Symptom: sudden increase in regional 5xx, latency p95 doubled for some heavy-chat customers, and increased cost due to fallback to larger cross-region variants.
- Customers: 23 customers experienced degraded QoS; 5 reported production errors.

What happened (brief):
A staggered decommission of several host pools in us-west-2 emitted decommission signals later than expected. Because the affinity hashing table still referenced the decommissioning hosts, new requests continued to be routed to them (affinity bleed). Those hosts were flagged by the node agent as degraded and promptly quarantined, pushing routing weight to the next tier that was not prepared to absorb sudden traffic. Our smart routing fallback policy uses a tier preference followed by variant fallbacks; when the preferred tier saturated, the control plane opted for immediate fallbacks to compatible model variants in distant regions rather than gradual spillover. This produced a cascading fallback surge that amplified load and latency.

Root cause analysis:
- Primary: delayed decommission signals from node agent due to batched heartbeat backlog in the autoscaler controller (a database write transaction retry created a 4–6s delay per node which accumulated across the node pool). This allowed affinity entries to remain valid longer than they should.
- Secondary: affinity table reconciliation runs had a long periodicity (5m) and relied on eventual eviction when node heartbeats dropped, so affinity entries were not proactively rebalanced.
- Tertiary: fallback policy had an aggressive failover threshold (immediate fallback after 2 consecutive rejections) and preferred variant compatibility over locality, causing cross-region spill instead of local tier-constrained queuing.

Immediate actions taken during incident:
- 07:45 UTC: Ops toggled a mitigation flag to disable automated cross-region variant fallbacks for affected customer routes, preventing further cross-region amplification.
- 07:50 UTC: We force-evicted stale affinity entries for the affected pools and triggered an emergency reconcile job to rebalance weights.
- 07:58 UTC: Autoscaler controller rollback applied to disable the batched heartbeat optimization until a fix was vetted.
- 08:05 UTC: Traffic gradually returned to steady-state; full service metrics normalized by 08:15 UTC.

Post-incident fixes implemented (short-term):
- Hotfix applied to autoscaler controller to remove the transaction retry pattern causing aggregated delays; reverted to a linear backoff with per-node isolation. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/1428)
- Reconcile frequency reduced from 5m to 45s for affinity table GC for tiers with high churn (config flag guard). (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/3180)
- Fallback policy adjusted: add adaptive cool-down and locality bias so fallbacks prefer same-region lower-capacity queues before cross-region variants. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/930)

Long-term actions and ownership:
- Replace batched heartbeat flow with streaming heartbeat pipeline and per-node ledger to avoid global transaction contention. Owner: infra/heartbeat team. Target milestone: runtime-1.27.
- Implement affinity snapshotting and fast-path reconciliation in the control plane so affinity invalidation occurs in reaction to quarantine signals rather than wait windows. Owner: routing team. Target milestone: runtime-1.27.
- Update fallback policy test harness with chaos tests that simulate delayed decommission signals, autoscaler delays, and region drain to validate non-amplifying behavior. Owner: sres/quality. Target milestone: runtime-1.28.
- Dashboarding: add an "affinity-bleed" alert rule combining high eviction rate + skewed tier weight delta + heartbeat latency. Owner: observability. ETA: 2 weeks.

Lessons learned and trade-offs:
- Aggressive cross-region fallbacks reduce request latencies for many failure modes but increase blast radius when upstream signals are noisy; we now bias toward locality for the first fallbacks.
- Batch/transaction optimizations can create emergent timing problems at scale; system-critical signaling paths need per-node isolation.

References and artifacts:
- Incident timeline & timeline notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-01-affinity-bleed
- PRs and code references listed above.
- Kibana dashboards: routing/affinity/us-west-2/2026-03-01
